title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Enveloped Viruses, Retroviruses and Antigenic Variation
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 4 · 8 questions · 82 marks · 28 parts · one mark per minute, so a little under an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording, and the paper, year and question number are named in the Sources block at the foot of every question. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in that same block.

Eight questions, 82 marks, 28 parts. The set is sized for coverage, not for the clock. Questions 1 to 5 are the influenza and HIV cycles, 50 marks; questions 6 to 8 are variation in viral genomes, 32 marks. Two sittings is a reasonable way to run it.

The anchors. Question 2 is JJC's 2017 Paper 3 Section B essay at its real 13 marks, and it is the full-cycle question: influenza end to end, five stages, plus how new strains arise. Question 4(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 11 word for word, which is the whole of learning outcome 2(e) compressed into one mark.

Four real figures. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing. Three further figures could not be recovered from their papers; those parts carry the paper's own description as prose instead, and say so.

No read-off-the-graph parts. Every figure here is stimulus for an identify or an explain, never for a trend description.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then asks you to justify every option, which for Question 6 means sorting mutation, recombination and reassortment one at a time.

The one line in your own notes that will cost you marks. Chapter 4.1 page 40 says antigenic shift can occur without undergoing genetic change. It cannot. The same chapter defines shift on page 38 as reassortment and states on page 43 that two or more viral strains are involved. Questions 6(b), 6(d) and 6(e) are built on exactly that distinction, and the schemes attached to them state the correction. A bird strain jumping straight to humans with no genetic change is direct cross-species transmission, not antigenic shift.

What else the marks reward. Write haemagglutinin and neuraminidase in full, because a scheme awards the full names and prints a reject for HA and NA. Say budding, not exocytosis. Say template and synthesis, never conversion. Write influenza's coat as nucleoprotein forming a nucleocapsid, not capsomeres. Say antigenic drift, never genetic drift. Give the shift-against-drift distinction as two or more strains against one strain and reassortment against point mutation.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required ANSWERS and not just for duplicated labels. Q1 what each labelled part of an influenza virion is for · Q2 the influenza cycle end to end, plus how mutation makes new strains · Q3 HIV, from why it is a retrovirus to what each of its enzymes does · Q4 the two cycles held side by side and counted · Q5 how an enveloped virus gets out, and what stops it · Q6 antigenic shift, and the strain count that is not optional · Q7 antigenic drift, from a missing exonuclease to a failed vaccine · Q8 four unfamiliar cases answered with machinery from other Books. Two pairs were checked closely and kept apart. Q1(a) explains what the influenza genome is for, while Q2 runs the genome through the cycle in order, and neither answer is the other. Q7(a) credits the missing proofreading exonuclease as the reason mutations arise, while Q7(b) rejects that same phrase by name because that stem makes the genome the subject and the polymerase is not a feature of the genome; the two parts exist to be held apart, and the schemes say so.

Nothing from Books 5 to 9, and nothing from Cluster 3. Antibodies, memory cells, vaccines and immunity are Extension Topic A and appear here only as the consequence of a changed antigen, never as the substance of an answer. Bacterial genetics is Cluster 3. Where the phage appears it is only as the other exit route, at the level of lysis against budding.
